facts.claim: 作者以共产主义者与裸体营的对话开场，把“读过马克思”压成椅子上留下的痕。
facts.quote: One turns to the other and asks, ‘Have you read Marx?’ The other replies, ‘Yes, it’s these wicker chairs.’

facts.claim: 莎士比亚进酒吧，门卫以 Bard（诗人/ barred 被拦）回敬。
facts.quote: William Shakespeare walks into a bar. The bouncer shouts, ‘You’re Bard!’

facts.claim: 作者用 E. M. Forster 的姓氏做“自愿/主动”的双关。
facts.quote: ‘My wife just read A Room With a View.’ ‘Forster?’ ‘No, she read it of her own accord.’

facts.claim: 福尔摩斯段子靠大写（喊）与小写（低声）的排版差，把 Lo, a case 读成 low, a case。
facts.quote: ‘I HAVE A MYSTERY FOR YOU, MR HOLMES!’ He looked at me and said ‘Lo, a case.’ ‘i have a mystery for you, mr holmes,’ i replied.

facts.claim: 同义词词典笑话以重复同一句 rubbish 来自我演示“没有同义词”。
facts.quote: My new thesaurus is rubbish. Not only that, but it’s also rubbish.

facts.claim: 造船书笑话把 riveting（铆接）与“引人入胜”叠在一词上。
facts.quote: I’m reading a book about how ships are built. It’s riveting!

facts.claim: 收尾用 Jane Austen 的小说名 Persuasion 兼指“被说服”。
facts.quote: My friend said she had never read anything by Jane Austen and probably never would. However, she was open to Persuasion.

relations.relation: “读马克思”与“藤椅在皮肤上留下的印子”同音，裸体营的设定让 marks 有了着落。
relations.quote: ‘Have you read Marx?’ The other replies, ‘Yes, it’s these wicker chairs.’

relations.relation: 叙述者大喊用全大写，福尔摩斯低声回话用全小写，字形本身承担了“小声”的语义。
relations.quote: ‘Lo, a case.’ ‘i have a mystery for you, mr holmes,’ i replied.

relations.relation: 条目式的同义词罗列替代了叙事，让“词典”成为笑话主体。
relations.quote: A thesaurus walks into a bar, pub, alehouse, saloon, tavern, watering hole, lounge and taproom.

relations.relation: stories 在图书馆语境里指楼层，作者用它冒充“故事”来贬低这家图书馆。
relations.quote: The library in town has three stories. Not a great library really.

numbers.meaning: 图书馆只有三层，stories 的双关由此成立。
numbers.quote: The library in town has three stories. Not a great library really.

numbers.meaning: 百万词小说写猛犸，mammoth undertaking 兼指“巨大工程”。
numbers.quote: I’m currently writing a million-word novel about a big hairy elephant passing in the left-hand lane of the motorway.

numbers.meaning: 作者拿 Williams 姐妹（Serena、Venus）与剧作家 Tennessee Williams 比拼“网球味”。
numbers.quote: There are at least two, Serena and Venus, that are way more tennisy.
